case_title: Phulel Singh v. State of Haryana
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B; IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (charged; acquitted of s.302 at trial)
weapon: None mentioned (kerosene alleged as the means of burning)
evidence_type: Dying declaration (recorded by Executive Magistrate); medical evidence; oral evidence of relatives, sarpanch and investigating officer
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.304-B IPC; 7 years rigorous imprisonment with fine; acquitted of s.302 IPC
high_court_outcome: Partly allowed: father-in-law acquitted of s.304-B; appellant's conviction and sentence upheld; State appeal and revision on s.302 dismissed
neutral_facts: The victim was married to the accused in 1987 and the couple had two children. The victim's family alleged that the accused harassed the victim because of insufficient dowry. The family said it had earlier paid cash and given a scooter and gold ornaments. Some days before Diwali in 1991, the victim's brother visited and the victim reportedly described dowry demands and ill-treatment. The victim's father approached the village sarpanch, who promised to counsel the in-laws after the festival. On the Diwali day, the victim was found burnt and was taken to a hospital in another city with about 91 per cent burns. The admitting doctor recorded that the victim said her husband had poured water to extinguish the fire. On 7 November the victim regained consciousness and told relatives the accused had set her on fire. The victim's relatives applied to a sub-divisional magistrate, and an Executive Magistrate recorded the victim's statement on 8 November after a doctor's fitness opinion. The statement attributed the burning to the accused and two in-laws, who had held the victim while kerosene was poured. An FIR was registered on that statement. The investigating officer concluded the case was not one of attempted murder or cruelty and found the victim was short-tempered. The victim later died, and a death report was sent to police on 18 November 1991.
physical_harm: Victim suffered about 91% burns and later died
financial_property_loss: Alleged dowry: Rs.20,000 cash, a scooter and gold ornaments (prosecution allegation, not a court finding)
motive: alleged: dowry demands and harassment for insufficient dowry
key_evidence_accepted: None relied on for conviction: dying declaration held not free from doubt; no proof of dowry harassment
witness_credibility: Relatives' evidence (PW-3, PW-4) scrutinised with caution; Executive Magistrate's admissions cast doubt on voluntariness; doctor's fitness examination doubtful; sarpanch did not mention dowry harassment
bail_history: Not stated (bail bonds referred to; grant or refusal not described)
trial_duration: offence: 5 November 1991 (burn injuries); trial judgment: 14 September 1999; High Court: 24 July 2009; Supreme Court: 27 September 2023
legal_representation: Accused: Rajul Bhargav, Sr. Adv., with Rajiv K. Garg, Ashish Garg, Lalit Nagar, T. L. Garg. State: Samar Vijay Singh, Raj Singh Rana, Keshav Mittal, Ms. Sabarni Som, Aman Dev Sharma, Pankaj Kumar Singh
investigation_status: FIR registered on dying statement; inquest held 19 November 1991; charge-sheet filed; committed to Sessions; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Dying declaration recorded after relatives' application; doctor's fitness opinion timed after statement; no entry in bed-head ticket
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted s.304-B, 7 years RI, acquitted s.302. High Court: partly allowed; appellant's conviction upheld. Supreme Court: appeal allowed; conviction set aside; appellant acquitted
prosecution_argument: Dying declaration reliable: recorded by Executive Magistrate and doctor certified fitness; relatives' and sarpanch's evidence proves dowry harassment beyond reasonable doubt
defence_argument: Dying declaration recorded days later and tutored by relatives; first information to doctor showed self-immolation; accused tried to extinguish fire; no evidence of dowry harassment; Makhan Singh relied on
legal_principle_applied: A conviction may rest solely on a dying declaration only if it is trustworthy, reliable and inspires confidence; dowry harassment must be proved beyond reasonable doubt
precedent_relied_upon: Makhan Singh v. State of Haryana, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1019 (referred to by defence)
other_sentence_order: Pending applications disposed of; bail bonds discharged
